caption:
Koko's fingers and knees feel stiff every morning lately. Many women notice more joint aches around menopause, as hormone changes can affect muscles, tendons and joints.

Research suggests strength training is one of the most useful tools at this stage, helping to maintain muscle and bone. Start with sit to stands from a chair, wall push-ups and band rows, 2–3 times a week, and build gradually. Keep walking and look after your sleep too.

A hot, swollen joint or aches with fever need your GP, and your GP is the place for broader menopause care. Our Chatswood and Sydney CBD physios can build a program that fits your life. Book online via the link in bio.
